judgments.V: Grammatically possible literal rendering; iniquity suggests wicked conduct rather than the Hebrew offense–consequence range. Weaker naturalness/contextual precision; does not transparently convey forgiveness.
judgments.Q: Serious alternative: Genesis50:17, Numbers14:19 and selected Greek support pardon/release interpretation. Implicit forgiver recoverable in address, but vv14–15 foreground consequences. Does not prove repentance.
judgments.L: Best immediate-context fit: announced livelihood loss/wandering, expulsion and danger, then divine protection. Numbers14:34 pairs bearing iniquities with forty-year consequences. Punishment resolves polysemy; I can supplies an implicit bearer, both contextually supported. Must disclose guilt/forgiveness.

limits: Contextual rendering preference, not unambiguous Hebrew or proved psychological state. Lamentations4:6 does not independently settle its own offense/punishment ambiguity.

identity_disclosure_after_freeze.L: Punishment proposal; already matches current lexical/theological preference but assessment did not see those fields.
